newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices up on foreign interest.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices up on foreign interest.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose on Wednesday, boosted by foreign buying, and dealers saw the state 2007 spread to the bund falling below 60 basis points.

"Since Monday midday there has been a good push behind Danish bonds and if Sweden and Italy can continue to hold their own against Germany the Danish-German spread could go under 60 basis points in the course of a week," a dealer said.

At 1330 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 112.30, yielding 6.12 percent, up from Tuesday's 112.12. The seven percent 2007, due to become the benchmark on September 1, rose to 104.95, yielding 6.32 percent, from 104.65.
Turnover in the benchmark was around 2.1 billion crowns at midday and in the 2007 about one billion.
The 2006 bond's yield gap to the 10-year bund narrowed one basis point to 44 bp and the 2007 gap to the bund shrank by the same amount to 65 basis points.
The crown was virtually unchanged at 3.8081 to the mark, compared to Tuesday's 3.8082.
The benchmark bond's September future rose 0.19 point to 115.55 with 561 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.25 point to 90.70.
